claims.text: Integrating first-principles phonon calculations with an expanded machine-learning model will improve prediction accuracy for low phonon thermal conductivity in equiatomic single-phase HEAs by at least 25%.
The framework will identify HEAs having room-temperature phonon thermal conductivity below 1.5 W/m·K.
Adding lattice-distortion and microstructural descriptors provides a more complete quantitative representation of phonon-scattering mechanisms.
Arc melting followed by homogenization annealing ensures minimal secondary phases in the proposed HEAs.
CoCrFeMnNi and its derivatives are examples within the proposed equiatomic single-phase HEA domain.
Configurational entropy and atomic-radius mismatch are established descriptors for HEA machine-learning models.
Models relying narrowly on compositional representations can have restricted generalization across HEA compositional space.
Multicomponent mixing in HEAs produces atomic-scale lattice distortion.
Nano- and mesoscale precipitates provide additional phonon-scattering sources.
Defects such as stacking faults or dislocation-like structures can scatter phonons.
Atomic-scale disorder preferentially scatters high-frequency phonons, while larger precipitates scatter lower-frequency phonons.
Enhanced lattice distortion increases phonon scattering and consequently reduces thermal conductivity.
The combined DFT–ML approach quantitatively captures lattice-distortion effects on phonon scattering.
Existing empirical or CALPHAD-based methods have lower accuracy for predicting ultralow thermal conductivity in HEAs.
The approach is applicable only to equiatomic, single-phase HEAs lacking significant intermetallic or secondary phases.
The framework is applicable to thermal-conductivity prediction from room temperature to 1200°C.
TDTR can provide the required thermal-conductivity measurements from room temperature through 1200°C for these alloys.
The hypothesis is falsified if more than one-third of tested compositions have measured thermal conductivity more than 30% above the predicted value.

contradictions.description: The applicability domain requires single-phase alloys with minimal or no significant secondary phases, yet the expanded model and proposed mechanism rely partly on secondary-phase indicators and nano-/mesoscale precipitates.
